### 4. restore-required-vs-build-conflation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `WorkspaceManager.cs:885-886` computes `restoreRequired` as the OR of `DetectRestoreRequired(projectStatuses)` (package-level NuGet check) and `HasRestoreRequiredWorkspaceDiagnostics(diagnosticsSink.Queue)`. `HasRestoreRequiredWorkspaceDiagnostics` (`:1409`) returns `true` when `WORKSPACE_UNRESOLVED_ANALYZER` is present — but that indicates a missing BUILD output (e.g. `ServerSurfaceCatalogAnalyzer.dll` not yet produced), not a missing NuGet package. This sets `session.RestoreRequired = true` (`:908`) when the real remedy is `dotnet build`. Downstream `WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto.BuildRestoreHint` (`WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto.cs:148-151`) checks `restoreRequired` first and emits "Run `dotnet restore`", sending callers into a no-op restore loop; `autoRestore=true` also fires a pointless restore. `workspace_readiness_report` (`WorkspaceTools.cs:655-678`) already distinguishes build-vs-restore via `HasBuildRequiredDiagnostic` — fixing `restoreRequired`'s computation eliminates the split-brain. Anchors verified: `WorkspaceManager.cs`, `WorkspaceTools.cs:76` (autoRestore) exist. |
| Approach | Three-file fix: (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs` — remove `WORKSPACE_UNRESOLVED_ANALYZER` from `HasRestoreRequiredWorkspaceDiagnostics`; add `private static bool HasBuildRequiredWorkspaceDiagnostics(IEnumerable<DiagnosticDto>)` checking for it; set a new `session.BuildRequired` field in `LoadIntoSessionAsync` (`:908` area); plumb `BuildRequired` in both `BuildStatus` overloads (`:1552/:1580`). (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/WorkspaceStatusDto.cs` — add `bool BuildRequired = false` (after `RestoreRequired`). (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto.cs` — add `bool BuildRequired`; in `From()` compute `buildRequired = status.BuildRequired`; update `BuildRestoreHint` to check `buildRequired` before `restoreRequired`, emitting "Run `dotnet build` on the analyzer project, then `workspace_reload`"; gate `isReady` on `!buildRequired`. `WorkspaceSession` inner class (same file) gains `public bool BuildRequired { get; set; }`. Test: extend `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceReadinessReportTests.cs` — update `ReadinessReport_UnresolvedAnalyzerBuildOutput_*` to assert `restoreRequired=false`, add `ReadinessReport_RestoreRequired_WithoutAnalyzerWarning_*` proving the NuGet path is unaffected. |
| Scope | Production files (3): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/WorkspaceStatusDto.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto.cs`. Test files (1): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceReadinessReportTests.cs` (extend existing class, +2 methods). Rule 3 (≤4 prod) and Rule 4 (≤3 test files) satisfied. `WorkspaceManager.cs` is a listed hotspot — no other hotspot-touching initiative should parallel-wave with this one. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | (1) `BuildRequired` propagates through both DTOs — ensure `workspace_health` (calls `workspace_status` internally) reflects the new field; check `SerializeWorkspaceLoadResult` in `WorkspaceTools.cs` for a projection that might shadow it. (2) `autoRestore` logic in `RestoreAndReloadIfRequiredAsync` must NOT trigger when only `BuildRequired=true` — verify the predicate gates only on `RestoreRequired`. (3) Removing `WORKSPACE_UNRESOLVED_ANALYZER` from the restore check may flip `restoreRequired=false` on a workspace with BOTH a missing NuGet package AND an unresolved analyzer — verify `DetectRestoreRequired(projectStatuses)` still independently fires (it reads `project.assets.json` directly). (4) Existing test passes `restoreRequired: true` to `CreateStatus`; after the fix the correct input is `restoreRequired: false, buildRequired: true`. |
| Validation | 1. `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` per file — zero new CS errors. 2. `dotnet test --filter "WorkspaceReadinessReportTests"` — all green incl. the 2 new/updated methods. 3. `dotnet test --filter "WorkspaceStatusSummaryDtoTests"` — no regressions. 4. Manual repro: load a workspace with an unbuilt analyzer dependency; assert `restoreRequired=false`, `buildRequired=true`, `restoreHint` contains "dotnet build", verdict "build-needed". 5. `dotnet test --filter "WorkspaceToolchainClassifierTests"`. 6. `./eng/verify-ai-docs.ps1`. |

### 5. worktree-teardown-windows-lock-multi-drain

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `workspace_close(drainProcesses=true)` at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/WorkspaceTools.cs:164-196` runs exactly one drain step: `dotnet build-server shutdown`. That terminates `VBCSCompiler.exe` and the MSBuild server but NOT `testhost.exe`/`vstest.console.exe`, which `dotnet test` (via `TestRunnerService`) spawns as independent children that can survive after `dotnet test` returns. The 2026-05-31 surface-test (teardown sub-phase 6z, server v2.3.1) confirmed that after a `build_workspace`/`test_run` sequence even multiple `build-server shutdown` drains left `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/bin/Debug/net10.0` locked; the lock cleared only after an explicit `testhost.exe` kill. No code in `src/` enumerates or terminates `testhost.exe`/`vstest.console` — `Process.GetProcessesByName` is absent from the codebase. `WorkspaceCloseDrainTests.cs` covers the build-server path but has no testhost-drain test. |
| Approach | Modify `WorkspaceTools.CloseWorkspace`: after the existing `build-server shutdown` await (`~:175`), add a second drain sub-step calling a new private static helper `TryKillDetachedTestHostsAsync(workingDirectory, logger, ct)`. The helper enumerates `Process.GetProcessesByName("testhost")` and `Process.GetProcessesByName("vstest.console")`, filters to processes whose `MainModule.FileName` starts with `workingDirectory` (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`), calls `process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` on each match, logs each kill at `Debug`, and swallows all exceptions with a `Debug` log — non-fatal, identical policy to the existing `build-server shutdown` catch. Guard `MainModule` access with try/catch (Windows access-denied is common); if `MainModule` is inaccessible, SKIP (do not kill-all — avoid killing unrelated IDE test runners). Inject a `Func<string, Process[]>` seam (mirror `DotnetCommandRunner._killProcessTree`) so the kill path is hermetically testable. Update the `workspace_close` description (`:114`) to mention "testhost.exe/vstest.console" alongside the MSBuild build-server. Extend `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceCloseDrainTests.cs` with `CloseWorkspace_DrainProcessesTrue_DoesNotLeakTesthostInWorkingDir` using the injected delegate to assert `Kill` is attempted for a worktree-scoped process stub. |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/WorkspaceTools.cs`. Test files modified (1, existing): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceCloseDrainTests.cs`. No new files. Rule 3 (1 prod file) and Rule 4 (0 new test files) satisfied. NOTE: `WorkspaceTools.cs` is a high-traffic tool file but is NOT on the addenda hotspot list (catalog/DI/WorkspaceManager); standard wave scheduling applies. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 28000 |
| Risks | (1) `Process.MainModule` throws `Win32Exception` (access denied) on protected processes; the catch-and-log handles it but the filter may silently skip inaccessible processes — document in code comments. (2) If VSTest spawns `testhost.exe` with a relocated working dir the path-prefix filter misses it — fall back to skip (not kill-all). (3) `vstest.console.exe` process name may vary by SDK version — keep additive (kill what matches, skip the rest). (4) Linux/macOS: `testhost` (no `.exe`) may appear; non-fatal policy keeps it safe. (5) Testability: the new kill path uses `Process.GetProcessesByName` directly — inject a delegate seam (same pattern as `DotnetCommandRunner._killProcessTree`) to keep tests hermetic. |
| Validation | 1. Existing `WorkspaceCloseDrainTests` all pass (no regression on build-server path). 2. New `CloseWorkspace_DrainProcessesTrue_DoesNotLeakTesthostInWorkingDir` passes — fake `getProcessesByName` returns a synthetic process stub for the worktree path; assert `Kill` called. 3. `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` on `RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio` and `RoslynMcp.Tests` — zero errors. 4. Manual smoke: `test_run` in a disposable worktree → `workspace_close(drainProcesses=true)` → `git worktree remove` succeeds without `Device or resource busy`. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness fix, teardown-only path. `Process.GetProcessesByName` runs once per `workspace_close(drainProcesses=true)`. |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | Fixed `workspace_close(drainProcesses=true)` to also terminate detached `testhost.exe`/`vstest.console` processes after `dotnet build-server shutdown`, resolving `git worktree remove` failures (`Device or resource busy`) that persisted after a `test_run` in a sweep worktree on Windows. |
| Backlog sync | Close rows: [worktree-teardown-windows-lock-multi-drain]. |
